one_liner: Fixed-size, heapless C++17 delegate beating std::function's invocation speed by 1.1-1.4x in a third-party benchmark.
what_it_does: Delegate is a std::function alternative for wrapping callables (function pointers, lambdas, functors) with a fixed, compile-time-sized storage buffer instead of type-erased heap allocation. API mirrors std::function closely: construct from a callable, call via operator(), test validity via explicit operator bool. Two variants: Delegate (FuncCopyable) for copyable captures, MoveDelegate (FuncNonCopyable) for move-only captures like unique_ptr.
how_it_is_fast: Never allocates: captured state is stored inline in a fixed-size aligned byte buffer (default 12 bytes, resizable via DELEGATE_ARGS_SIZE macro), so there is no heap round-trip on construction, copy, move, or destruction. Dispatch uses a raw function pointer plus a small static per-type vtable (copy/move/destroy) built once via templates, avoiding the extra indirection and RTTI/exception bookkeeping std::function implementations carry. No dynamic memory management and no exception-safety machinery to execute on the hot call path.
when_to_use: Callback/handler slots where the callable's capture state is small and known ahead of time (fits in ~12-20 bytes, adjustable via DELEGATE_ARGS_SIZE)
Hot paths that construct/copy/destroy callables frequently and need to avoid heap allocation and its jitter
Embedded or latency-sensitive code that wants predictable, allocation-free memory behavior
Code that already avoids RTTI/exceptions and does not need std::function's arbitrary-size type erasure
Move-only captures (e.g. unique_ptr) via the MoveDelegate variant, where std::function historically disallows or complicates this
when_not_to_use: Captures larger than the fixed buffer size — code fails to compile (static_assert), unlike std::function's silent heap fallback
Codebases that rely on std::function's RTTI/exception interplay or allocator-aware construction
Projects needing an OSI-approved license: this ships a custom permissive header notice, not MIT/Apache/BSD
Long-term maintenance risk: repo has been inactive since 2022-07-27 and only 43 stars
Multi-threaded use without external synchronization — no thread-safety guarantees are documented or implemented

integration.dependencies: none for the library itself (Catch2 is a test-only dependency for delegate_ut.cpp)
integration.platforms: not documented (no platform-specific code observed; standard C++17, no intrinsics)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; no synchronization primitives in delegate.h, so treat as not thread-safe without external locking
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: constructor/call/bool syntax mirrors std::function, but capture size is fixed at compile time (static_assert on overflow instead of heap fallback), and there is no support for RTTI, exceptions, or allocators

gotchas: Default capture buffer is only sizeof(int)+sizeof(int*) (12 bytes on typical 64-bit builds), plus 8 bytes of vtable/call-pointer overhead; override via #define DELEGATE_ARGS_SIZE / DELEGATE_ARGS_ALIGN before including the header if captures don't fit

Copying a Delegate built from a non-copyable functor calls std::terminate() at runtime rather than failing to compile (only FuncCopyable's copy path is affected; use MoveDelegate to avoid this class of captures entirely)
No exception awareness at all — the header does not catch or propagate exceptions from the wrapped callable differently than a normal call would
No LICENSE file; licensing is a custom notice embedded in the delegate.h comment block requiring the comment block to remain in derived works
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Delegate over stdext::inplace_function or SmallFunction when you want the smallest reported invocation times in this same benchmark suite for pointer/lambda-heavy call patterns; pick stdext::inplace_function instead if you need an OSI-approved (SG14/Boost-style) license, since Delegate's license is a non-standard permissive notice.
verified_claims_summary: On MSVC 15.9.4 (Visual Studio, 64-bit Release, Boost 1.69.0, CPU unspecified) in jamboree/CxxFunctionBenchmark's various.cpp, Delegate beat MSVC STL's std::function in all 7 invocation categories (e.g. function_pointer 0.210s vs 0.264s, ~1.26x; compile_time_function_pointer 0.132s vs 0.188s, ~1.42x), and was the fastest of 13 implementations in 5 of 7 categories (stdex::function and func::function tied or edged it out in heavy_functor and lambda_capture).
status_note: Abandoned since the last commit on 2022-07-27; usability is 'reference' because the custom header license is not OSI-approved, though the code is small (~350 lines) and easy to vendor or re-license by copying and adapting.
